reference: Context parameterization in Retrieval-Augmented Generation encodes context into a small set of trainable parameters, such as LoRA adapters or soft prompts, which are plugged into a frozen LLM and optimized using context-related objectives like QA-style training or supervised next-token prediction. This method allows the model to access contextual information via these internal parameters at inference time rather than explicitly attending to external context tokens. Consequently, this substantially reduces inference costs because the input sequence only contains the task instruction, and it enables the incorporation of long contexts that would otherwise exceed the model's context window limit.

Overall, this work is positioned at the intersection of multilingual RAG, grounding-aware evaluation, and low-resource language processing.
